Validate the filings once, and carry the work along

Source: R/xbrl_validate.R
xbrl_validate.Rd

Standardises the facts and runs everything the analysis functions need – who each company is, the checks of the three statements, and the statements line by line on both bases – and returns the facts with that work attached. xbrl_screen(), xbrl_panel(), xbrl_lines() and xbrl_report_data() read it instead of doing it again, so a pipeline pays for the expensive part once:

Usage

xbrl_validate(x)

Arguments

x

A tibble from read_xbrl().

Value

x, standardised by xbrl_standardise(), of class cvrr_validated, with the work in attr(v, "validated"): company (xbrl_company() without prose), statement, cascade and cashflow (the checks), lines (from xbrl_lines(), by basis and statement) and the fingerprints.

Details

v <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl") |>
  xbrl_validate()
s <- xbrl_screen(v)
p <- xbrl_panel(v)
xbrl_report(xbrl_report_data(v, cvr = "12345678"), "12345678.html")

Why the facts and not a panel

A panel is one row per company and year and a few dozen variables, and that is a view, not the data. It leaves out the dimensions and the notes, every line beyond its variables, where each figure came from – reported, derived or corrected – the comparatives the unit check reads, and the auditor's text. So the validated object stays the facts, one row per fact as read_xbrl() gave them, and the panel is cut from it when asked for.

It is an ordinary tibble, and everything that takes facts takes it.

When the work still applies

The work is per filing, so a subset of whole filings keeps it: v[v$cvr == "12345678", ] is still validated, for that company. Each filing's facts are fingerprinted – the number of rows and the sum of the values – and a filing whose facts no longer match is not trusted: change a value, or drop some of a filing's rows, and the functions do the work again from the facts as they stand. Nothing stale is read, and nothing has to be remembered.

Standardising compares a filing with the company's later filings, and that comparison was made on everything validated together. A subset keeps its corrections, which were made with more information than the subset has.
